overview: Rika’s unique setting controls how quickly her first normal attack turns toward a secondary target.
technicalOverview: Rika (CN_041) has one populated unique row: zero-based CharacterUniqueDataTable3 row 0 named CN_040. Its only nonzero value is float 0 = 180, used directly as the turn-time divisor when her first normal attack steers toward a valid secondary target. The remaining zero floats are positions that shared camera and AI helpers know how to read, but no active CN_041 caller was found for them; generic projection-sorcery damage fallback can also read float 0. CN_041 uses its own UCN_041 action controller, a behavior override that makes the cursed-energy AI action a one-shot Idle executor, and a bone controller that disables several skeleton systems; its Super retargeting and grounded attack effects do not consume this row.

CN_040.title: Rika's shared CN_040-named unique row (CharacterUniqueDataTable3 row 0)
CN_040.overview: This row contains the 180 homing-turn divisor at value index 0 and zeros everywhere else. It is reached through the raw owner accessor UniqueRows[0]->FloatValue[n], with no bounds or null checks. The shared camera builder would read values 0-10 if called with row 0, but CN_041's actions and controller do not call it; the generic AI timed-hold executors read values 0-2, but CN_041 replaces their 0x11 slot with a non-timed Idle executor.

0.label: Homing turn-time divisor
0.simple: Controls how long Rika's first normal attack spends turning toward a secondary target. A larger number makes the computed turn time smaller; changing it to zero or a negative value disables that turn instead of making it instant.
0.technical: Traced use: all eight custom normal-attack classes built by UCN_041_ActionController::CreateAction inherit TCN_041_NormalAttack::StartAttackHoming. On start count 0, a valid secondary target, and a controller that is UCN_041_ActionController, they call UGameCharacterActionController::SteerTowardSecondaryTarget(&ActionElapsedTime). That helper rechecks target validity, takes the unsigned angle in degrees between the owner's forward and the safe-normalized 2-D target delta, reads GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue(0, 0), and requires the value to be strictly greater than 0. Otherwise it writes 0 and does not rotate. On success it writes turnTime = angle / 180 and calls RotateTowardLocation(target location, turnTime, Linear, 2.0f). Secondary read: the inherited generic ProjectionSorceryReceive action uses this same owner row 0 float 0 as RestraintTime only when the incoming DamageTableRow pointer is null; it advances ActionElapsedTime and triggers the stagger/cleanup when RestraintTime <= ActionElapsedTime. The generic timed-hold AI executors also read float 0 as a base duration, but CN_041's behavior factory does not instantiate those Hold executors.

1.label: Shared camera X-side offset / unused AI hold scale
1.simple: No active CN_041 use was found. Generic code can use this as a camera side-offset or as a level-scaled AI hold duration, but neither path is taken by this character's traced setup.
1.technical: FGameCharacterAction::MakeUniqueCameraRequest(CameraMode=2, RowIndex) reads FloatValue[1] as Request.CameraOffset.Y; CN_041 has no call to that helper in its controller or action classes. FGameCharacterAIAction_CursedEnergyAttack1Hold::Reset reads FloatValue[0] + FloatValue[1] * CursedEnergyLevel, but UCN_041_BehaviorController::CreateThinkParam replaces ordinal 0x11 with FGameCharacterAIAction_CursedEnergyAttack1Idle, and the base factory creates no Hold executor. The current 0 is not evidence that the slot is inherently unused.

2.label: Shared camera height offset / unused AI hold scale
2.simple: No active CN_041 use was found. Generic code can use this as a camera vertical offset or as a level-scaled cursed-energy-2 hold duration; CN_041 does not reach either path.
2.technical: MakeUniqueCameraRequest(2, RowIndex) reads FloatValue[2] as Request.CameraOffset.Z. FGameCharacterAIAction_CursedEnergyAttack2Hold::Reset reads FloatValue[0] + FloatValue[2] * CursedEnergyLevel, but CN_041's behavior factory does not create that Hold executor and the action controller explicitly rejects CursedEnergyAttack_2 / CursedEnergyAttackAir_2 requests.

3.label: Shared camera lower-angle limit
3.simple: No active CN_041 use was found; a shared camera helper would assign this to the lower angle limit if a CN_041 action requested camera mode 2 with row 0.
3.technical: MakeUniqueCameraRequest reads Owner row FloatValue[3] into Request.LimitAngleDown only when CameraMode == 2. No CN_041 action or controller call site passes row 0 to that helper.

4.technical: MakeUniqueCameraRequest reads FloatValue[4] into Request.LimitAngleUp only when CameraMode == 2. No CN_041 caller was traced.

7.label: Shared camera FOV easing selector

7.technical: MakeUniqueCameraRequest casts FloatValue[7] to int32 and maps exactly 0 -> Linear, 1 -> EaseIn, 2 -> EaseOut, 3 -> EaseInOut; any other value leaves FieldOfViewEasing at its default. This occurs only for CameraMode == 2 and no CN_041 caller was traced.

notes.text: The accessor is a raw unchecked array dereference: RowIndex selects UniqueRows and ValueIndex selects that row's FloatValue. Row 0 is valid for CN_041, and FloatValue has 14 entries; values 11-13 have no identified row-0 read in the shared helper or in CN_041's own code.

The row name CN_040 is data reuse, not an instruction to use UCN_040_ActionController. CN_041 uses UCN_041_ActionController, while the similarly named CN_040 controller is a shikigami-family controller.

No trap or spawner forwarding from CN_041 was found. The generic trap GetUniqueFloat forwards to a trap source actor's interface, but CN_041's controller and action source contain no trap/spawner calls; do not mix in trap unique tables.

Normal attacks 1, 1_1, 2, 3_1 and their air variants are all custom CN_041 classes. Their first-start steering is what gives float 0 its ordinary effect; later starts use the base attack tick instead.

The Super attack is separate from this row's main use: its first start zeroes cursed energy and can add the owner as a focus candidate; finish effects request the event state on the second finish and repick the target by lowest hit-point ratio (or nearest unlocked target if that one is collision-locked). No unique float is read in those bodies.

AI setup is CN_041-specific: EGameCharacterAIType::CN_041 creates FGameCharacterAIThinkNode_CN_041, and its Tick only adjusts AI state value 0 for an active Super or empty HP. The behavior controller overrides ordinal 0x11 with the one-shot CursedEnergyAttack1Idle executor, which presses the key when idle and clears input otherwise; it has no unique-row read.

CN_041's attack notify effects are grounded trace/spawn effects named FX_CN_040_00301_1, _2 and _3. They use the notify's FloatParameter as the trace half-height and a shared shot-blocker object list; they do not read CharacterUnique row values.

Movement and skeleton quirks are controller code, not row values: Run and NormalDash force move modes 4 and 8 at start; Down and DownEnd always use face-down animation names; the bone controller resolves both ankle bones to 'hip', empties foot IKs, and folds lean/aim-offset/foot-bend updates to no-ops.

The reconstruction status is mixed: the row lookup and normal-attack homing helper are source-traced, but CN_041's Super slot-3 effect path is documented as a formerly blocked helper in the verification note. Treat any gameplay interpretation beyond the traced formulas as observed, not proven balance intent.
